entry.title: AI is already massively speeding up AI research (9 minute read)
entry.content:
AI companies are not ready to handle the risks of recursive self-improvement safely and responsibly, despite having talked about them for years, and this is incredibly dangerous. Policymakers need to make it a top priority to rapidly understand these risks, and consider pausing or pacing frontier AI progress. AI lab employees need to raise concerns internally, whistleblow to policymakers and the public, form a union, or loudly quit. Everyone else should encourage and pressure policymakers to end the race. Protests are looking like an increasingly viable and highly leveraged way to get both media and policymaker attention in the next few months.

entry.title: What comes after AGI? (18 minute read)
entry.content:
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is now within reach, so we can no longer put off seriously considering what will come next. AI achieving artificial general superintelligence (ASI) will have a profound impact on science, the economy, and society at a scale much greater than AGI itself. Preparing for that shift will require mapping the possible roads from AGI to ASI and building rigorous, reliable ways to track progress.

entry.title: Why Antigravity Eats Weekly Quota Fast - and What I Measured (17 minute read)
entry.content:
Google Antigravity wipes users' prompt caches if there is a 5-minute pause. Refreshing the cache just before expiry works, but only for 3 pings. Even a 5-word prompt starts with 13,800 to 16,800+ tokens of system instructions, MCP schemas, and skills. Disabling unused MCP servers and plugins shrinks cold turns and cache misses.

entry.title: Switching LLMs mid-conversation is a ski-rental problem (30 minute read)
entry.content:
Most work on routing between language models is centered on making sure the right model handles the right request. A classifier scores the request, then the request is routed to a cheap model if it is easy, and a frontier model if it is hard. For coding agents, this is only half of the problem. The second half of the problem is knowing when a running session should change model. This problem, which this post discusses, has a classic form: the ski-rental problem.
Discuss on TLDR →

entry.title: Introducing Model Factory (8 minute read)
entry.content:
Model Factory is a training loop that lets any company train, deploy, and continuously improve models in production. It brings reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning, pre-training, and inference together into one control plane. It also offers health checks, automatic node replacement, and recovery from the latest checkpoint for long-running experiments. Model Factory has already been deployed for teams working on finance automation, computer use, scientific discovery, chip design, and other industries.

entry.title: Quickly, There's No Time (38 minute read)
entry.content:
Many things point to the substantial possibility of superintelligence arriving next year. Any plan to prepare for this has to be ready for the full automation of AI R&D, which will result in the rapid advancement of AI abilities beyond human levels. It will need to include mechanisms to slow down the resulting growth in capabilities.

entry.title: The Silent Consensus (15 minute read)
entry.content:
The most common vision for the future that AI brings isn't totally positive. It is often left unsaid, discernible only by implication, a silent consensus. The decisions humans make will likely lead to a world in which people have forfeited effective authority over much of our civilization. Even if we make extraordinary progress on AI safety and alignment, we could still find ourselves having submitted to a machine entity.

entry.title: World 2030 (8 minute read)
entry.content:
Predicting how AI will affect the economy requires looking at all of the different components of that economy and figuring out how they might affect each other. World 2030 is a study that sets up nine groups (AI labs, big employers, banks and insurers, utilities, startups, universities, workers, governments, and the Fed) and runs the US economy forward in six-month turns to 2030. It aimed to identify both the invariants and the boundaries of what can change as these powerful forces interact with each other. The study predicts that AI will break per-seat software pricing and cut US junior desk hiring.

entry.title: Unlocking Stable On-Policy RL on TPU with Bitwise-Zero Train–Inference Mismatch (7 minute read)
entry.content:
Google's ZERO-TIM implementation, verified across 64 TPU v5p chips, achieves bitwise-identical logprobs for sampler and trainer, ensuring true on-policy stability in RL training by eliminating numerical discrepancies. This solution addresses floating-point addition errors in separate serving and training paths, using consistent arithmetic operations and standardized reduction orders across TPU meshes.

entry.title: On the Brutality of Amdahl's Law (12 minute read)
entry.content:
The world is far too slow to see the high double-digit or more economic growth and seismic transformations in the economy that AI is predicted to bring. Intelligence isn't the only technology curve to go quasi-infinite in the last century and a half. Electricity, communication, computers, transportation, and agriculture have all experienced extreme growth and transformation. Despite this, we've only seen 2% GDP per capita growth for nearly 150 years.

entry.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)
entry.content:
A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.

entry.title: What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)
entry.content:
Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

From TLDR AI · 2026-11-10 · Engineering & Research

entry.title: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling (28 minute read)
entry.content:
Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.

This proof shows quantum computers are not exponentially faster on random inputs compared to classical ones, resolving a significant question about quantum speedups.

entry.content:
Ace is a tool for building software together, locally. It allows developers to collaborate with agents and their teams, all from their own machine. Teams can work together without exposing anything to the public internet.
